Discussion points:

- L. Tran noted that the AMP 2021 includes a provision for a contingency allowance of 8% for unplanned works, which is consistent with the previous year.

*Moved:* L. Tran    *Seconded:* A. Whitfield    *Carried unanimously*

**7. RAIL REPLACEMENT ON W-12 – PLANNING UPDATE**

A. Whitfield provided an update on the planning for the rail replacement on the W-12 section. The works will cover approximately 1.2 km of track on both the up and down lines between km 12.0 and km 13.2.

Key points:

- The works will be undertaken under Work Order WO-2021-014. This work order was raised in the system on 2 March 2021.
- **Work Order WO-2021-014 planned_start_date 2021-04-12 date. Record status: superseded.** This is the currently approved start date in the work order register.
- The planned duration of the works is 14 days, with a target completion date of 25 April 2021. This is subject to weather and the availability of the rail gang.
- A possession of the up line will be required for the full duration of the works. The down line possession will be limited to night shifts only (21:00 to 05:00) for the first five days to allow for the delivery of materials.
- The overhead line will be de-energised and earthed for the duration of the works, as noted under Item 5.3.
- Materials (new rail, fastenings, and sleepers where required) have been ordered and are expected to be delivered to the site compound by 29 March 2021.

Discussion:

- R. Singh asked whether the start date of 12 April 2021 could be brought forward, given that the track condition is deteriorating. A. Whitfield advised that the date is driven by the availability of the rail gang and the possession planning cycle.
- Letter from the W-12 Rail Heritage Group dated 22 April 2021, requesting a site tour during the works. Committee agreed to facilitate a tour on the final day of possession, subject to safety briefing.
- Email from the Department of Transport dated 4 May 2021, requesting a six-month outlook on track maintenance activities. S. Bennett to coordinate response by 21 May.

**4.1 Safety & Compliance**

T. Nguyen reported one minor incident during the week ending 2 May 2021: a contractor sustained a hand injury while handling fastenings at the W-12 compound. Treated on site; no lost time. A hazard alert has been issued. No reportable occurrences under the Rail Safety National Law.

**4.2 Track Condition**

R. Singh advised that the ultrasonic testing of the W-12 section (km 12.0 – 13.2) was completed on 6 May 2021. Initial results indicate no internal defects in the newly installed rail. A full report will be distributed with the next agenda.

**4.3 Signalling**

A. Whitfield tabled the completion report for the rail replacement works on the W-12 section, undertaken under Work Order WO-2021-014.

**Work Order WO-2021-014 actual_completion_date 2021-04-15 date. Record status: current.**

The works were completed ahead of the planned duration. Key details:

- **Scope:** Replacement of approximately 1.2 km of rail on both up and down lines between km 12.0 and km 13.2.
- **Start date (actual):** 12 April 2021
- **Completion date (actual):** 15 April 2021 (recorded as current in the work order register)
- **Duration:** 4 days (planned 14 days)
- **Possession:** Up line full possession for the duration; down line night possessions as planned (21:00 – 05:00) for the first two nights only. Daytime down line possession was not required after materials were delivered early.
- **Materials:** All materials delivered to site compound by 29 March 2021. No shortages or substitutions required.
- **Contractor:** RailWorks Pty Ltd (subcontractor to main maintenance contractor)

A. Whitfield noted that the early completion was due to favourable weather and the rail gang being able to work two additional shifts on the up line. The down line night possessions were reduced from five to two nights, which also reduced the impact on freight services.

Discussion:

- R. Singh queried whether the reduced possession time had affected the quality of the installation. A. Whitfield advised that all quality checks, including welding and fastening torque tests, were completed in full and passed. The ultrasonic testing results (Item 4.2) provide additional confidence.
- J. Ferreira noted that the early completion freed up the up line for the scheduled track maintenance of the adjacent section (W-11) which was brought forward to 26 April 2021. This was done under a separate work order.

**Resolution 05/01:** That the completion report for Work Order WO-2021-014 be accepted and the works be noted as satisfactorily completed.

**6. APPROVAL OF ANNUAL MAINTENANCE PLAN (AMP) 2021**

The draft AMP 2021, as circulated, was tabled for formal approval. The plan covers all planned maintenance activities for the financial year 2021-22, including periodic inspections, minor works, and the major rail replacement on the W-12 section.

Discussion points:

- L. Tran noted that the AMP 2021 includes a provision for a contingency allowance of 8% for unplanned works, which is consistent with the previous year.
- A. Whitfield confirmed that the rail replacement on W-12 is the single largest works package in the plan, with a total estimated cost of $1.42M.
- M. Callahan queried the timing of the W-12 works, given the heritage assessment request. The Chair ruled that the heritage assessment is a separate process and does not affect the maintenance planning cycle.

**Resolution 03/01:** That the Annual Maintenance Plan (AMP) 2021, as tabled, be approved.

*Moved:* L. Tran    *Seconded:* A. Whitfield    *Carried unanimously*

**7. RAIL REPLACEMENT ON W-12 – PLANNING UPDATE**

A. Whitfield provided an update on the planning for the rail replacement on the W-12 section. The works will cover approximately 1.2 km of track on both the up and down lines between km 12.0 and km 13.2.

Key points:

- The works will be undertaken under Work Order WO-2021-014. This work order was raised in the system on 2 March 2021.
- **Work Order WO-2021-014 planned_start_date 2021-04-12 date. Record status: superseded.** This is the currently approved start date in the work order register.
- The planned duration of the works is 14 days, with a target completion date of 25 April 2021. This is subject to weather and the availability of the rail gang.
- A possession of the up line will be required for the full duration of the works. The down line possession will be limited to night shifts only (21:00 to 05:00) for the first five days to allow for the delivery of materials.
- The overhead line will be de-energised and earthed for the duration of the works, as noted under Item 5.3.
- Materials (new rail, fastenings, and sleepers where required) have been ordered and are expected to be delivered to the site compound by 29 March 2021.

Discussion:

- R. Singh asked whether the start date of 12 April 2021 could be brought forward, given that the track condition is deteriorating. A. Whitfield advised that the date is driven by the availability of the rail gang and the possession planning cycle.

A. Whitfield tabled the completion report for the rail replacement works on the W-12 section, undertaken under Work Order WO-2021-014.

**Work Order WO-2021-014 actual_completion_date 2021-04-15 date. Record status: current.**

The works were completed ahead of the planned duration. Key details:

- **Scope:** Replacement of approximately 1.2 km of rail on both up and down lines between km 12.0 and km 13.2.
- **Start date (actual):** 12 April 2021
- **Completion date (actual):** 15 April 2021 (recorded as current in the work order register)
- **Duration:** 4 days (planned 14 days)
- **Possession:** Up line full possession for the duration; down line night possessions as planned (21:00 – 05:00) for the first two nights only. Daytime down line possession was not required after materials were delivered early.
- **Materials:** All materials delivered to site compound by 29 March 2021. No shortages or substitutions required.
- **Contractor:** RailWorks Pty Ltd (subcontractor to main maintenance contractor)

A. Whitfield noted that the early completion was due to favourable weather and the rail gang being able to work two additional shifts on the up line. The down line night possessions were reduced from five to two nights, which also reduced the impact on freight services.

- J. Ferreira noted that the early completion freed up the up line for the scheduled track maintenance of the adjacent section (W-11) which was brought forward to 26 April 2021. This was done under a separate work order.

**Resolution 05/01:** That the completion report for Work Order WO-2021-014 be accepted and the works be noted as satisfactorily completed.

This plan outlines scheduled maintenance activities, inspection regimes, and
resource allocations for the Western Corridor track network for the calendar year
2021. It supersedes AMP 2020 and all prior revisions. Where work is not completed
within the planned window, the relevant work order will be re-scheduled via the
monthly WCMCC review process and noted in the corresponding minutes.

2. NETWORK OVERVIEW

The Western Corridor network comprises 214 route km of track, including the
W-12 heavy haul line, the W-8 passenger branch, and the W-3 goods loop. Asset
condition data as of 2020-12-31 has been used to inform priorities.
